title: Infections and antimicrobials in the ICU

steps.tx: When **extended spectrum beta lactamase** organisms are likely, septic shock from a urinary or abdominal source is started on a carbapenem or on piperacillin tazobactam. You should narrow the drug once the culture has returned. A broad start is a bridge, not a month of the same agent. Do not keep the carbapenem because the first day was frightening. Source control still has to happen. The culture, not habit, chooses the final agent.

steps.tx: **Carbapenem resistant Enterobacterales** are treated with a drug the isolate is susceptible to. Ceftazidime avibactam is one choice when the mechanism matches that drug. Dual carbapenem therapy is not a default. Two carbapenems do not invent a new enzyme inhibitor. Read the report, then pick one active agent. A second drug needs a reason you can name. Anxiety is not that reason.

left.title: What to do
points: Use a drug the isolate is susceptible to
Ceftazidime avibactam when the mechanism matches
One active agent is the start

right.title: What not to do
points: Dual carbapenem therapy as a default
Add a second drug from anxiety

steps.tx: **Acinetobacter** treatment follows the susceptibility report. Colistin is a last resort, because it injures the kidney and it reaches the lung poorly. Source control of an infected line or a collection matters more than adding a third drug. The drawing is ventilator associated pneumonia, a common site for this organism. Do not add a drug to a report you have not read. A dead collection will not improve because the prescription got longer.

vis.alt: Intubated airway with subglottic secretions, cuff microaspiration, luminal biofilm, purulent bronchitis and alveolar consolidation.
vis.caption: Cuff microaspiration, luminal biofilm and alveolar consolidation. This is the lung site. Colistin levels and the susceptibility report are not drawn (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Invasive candidiasis** is suspected in a septic patient who has risk factors and does not improve on antibacterial drugs. An echinocandin is the empiric start. Fluconazole is for a susceptible isolate in a patient who is stable. Do not open with fluconazole while the patient is in shock. A yeast in the sputum of a ventilated patient is often colonisation. Blood cultures and the bedside picture decide whether you treat.

rows: Use it as the shock regimen

steps.tx: A **central line associated bloodstream infection** is prevented by a checklist. Use a sterile insertion, chlorhexidine on the skin, and a daily review of whether the line is still needed. Remove the line when it is the source. The drawing shows erythema and purulence at the insertion site, with paired blood cultures. A new line placed through the same infected tract is not source control. The checklist fails if nobody asks, today, whether the line can come out.

vis.alt: Central line with erythema and purulence at the insertion site, and paired catheter and peripheral blood cultures.
vis.caption: Insertion-site infection and paired blood cultures. The sterile checklist and the chlorhexidine step are not drawn (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Catheter associated urinary** infection is avoided by taking the urinary catheter out. A positive culture without symptoms is colonisation, and it is not treated, except in pregnancy or before a urological procedure. Do not answer an old catheter with an antibiotic. If a catheter must stay, change it and send a fresh specimen. Treating colonisation breeds resistance. The culture is a result. It is not an instruction.

right.title: Do not treat
points: A positive culture and no symptoms

steps.tx: **Procalcitonin** can support a decision to stop antibiotics when the clinical course is already good. It does not start antibiotics, and it does not overrule a concerning examination. Use it as one more piece of a recovery you can already see. A falling number in a patient who is worse is not permission to stop. The poster agrees that the test never overrides the clinical picture. Look at the patient before you look at the assay.

vis.alt: Flowchart of ICU antibiotic reassessment, de-escalation when cultures are negative, and escalation when treatment fails.
vis.caption: Reassessment, de-escalation, and a note that procalcitonin never overrides the examination. The poster also prints a 7 day pneumonia course and an older vancomycin trough of 15 to 20. Those boxes are the drawing, not a dosing order (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Augmented renal clearance** is a creatinine clearance above about 130 mL per minute, often in a young trauma or neurosurgical patient. Renally cleared antibiotics are then underdosed. Raise the dose, or measure a level. A normal creatinine does not mean a normal clearance. A kidney that is clearing fast hides inside a tidy lab number. Check the clearance. Do not trust the creatinine line on its own.

rows: Increase the dose or measure a level
Do not assume a standard dose
Can still hide a fast clearance
Do not use creatinine as the clearance
